subject: An Important Safety Message and Virtual Training Notice from Rutgers Police
body:
Members of the Rutgers Community:


University Public Safety is committed to working in partnership with students, faculty, and staff to provide a safe, enjoyable, and fulfilling university experience. To better prepare the community for emergency situations, we are offering a virtual Workplace Violence and Active Shooter Preparedness training session. Vincent DeNota, director of security services for the Rutgers University Police Department, will discuss key elements of prevention and mitigation strategies to utilize in the event of an emergency. The 45-minute training will be held virtually on Wednesday, November 13, 2024, at 10:00 am and is designed for faculty and staff who have not received formal in-person instruction.



Registration is required. Please follow the link below to register for this training session.

https://rutgers.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_UmSCdDcRQ32t5FDER-EeZg


  *   To enhance classroom security in an emergency, Rutgers University began installing locking mechanisms in 2022. Currently, 35% of the total classrooms across all campuses have new thumb latch locks installed.  This is an ongoing university-wide process that is complex and requires large scale collaborative efforts.  The project is expected to be completed in the fall of 2026. Additional information regarding this process and operation of thumb latch locks can be found at https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/iam/classroom-locks.
  *   You can take an active approach in your personal preparedness by viewing the University's Emergency<http://emergency.rutgers.edu/> Action Plans<http://emergency.rutgers.edu/> and observing noted precautions we have outlined on our website<https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/crime-prevention>.<https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/crime-prevention> Please also review our Active Shooter Resources<https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/active-shooter> for resources and guidelines that are intended to reduce your personal risk in the event of an active shooter situation. RUPD officers are trained and equipped to respond to a myriad of emergency service calls inclusive of active shooter.
  *   During emergencies, accurate information is important. To receive up-to-date text alerts, please be sure to register or update your emergency notification information by visiting http://ens.rutgers.edu<http://ens.rutgers.edu/>.<http://ens.rutgers.edu/> All university students, faculty, staff, and guests who are subscribed to the emergency notification system are also encouraged to download Rave Guardian, a free mobile safety app designed to keep you connected to the Rutgers University Police Department and enable you to access important campus safety resources. Additional information and FAQs are outlined on our Text to RUPD website<https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/rupd/text>.<https://ipo.rutgers.edu/publicsafety/rupd/text>
  *   The RUPD supports the "Concerned? Do Something!<https://studentconduct.rutgers.edu/report-concern>" initiative and reminds you to report behaviors that concern you. The primary purpose of sharing a concern is to help prevent personal, emotional, psychological, academic, and substance abuse issues from getting worse, especially when someone is perceived to be a danger to themselves or others.


Community Police Officers offer educational programs upon request on a host of different topics including, but not limited to personal safety, active shooter awareness, and crime prevention. To schedule an informational session please contact the following RUPD command staff personnel:



1.       Rutgers University-Camden: Captain Matthew Gulsby by phone at 856-225-6885 or email at matthew.gulsby@rutgers.edu<mailto:matthew.gulsby@rutgers.edu>

2.       Rutgers University-Newark and Rutgers Biomedical and Health Sciences (RBHS) at Newark: Captain Michael Shoulars by phone at 973-972-2003 or email at michael.shoulars@rutgers.edu<mailto:michael.shoulars@rutgers.edu>

3.       Rutgers University-New Brunswick (including RBHS at New Brunswick/Piscataway): Acting Captain John Bell by phone at 848-932-4881 or email at john.bell@rutgers.edu<mailto:john.bell@rutgers.edu>





Working together, we can enhance safety and security at Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey.


Kenneth Cop
Vice President / Public Safety
Chief of University Police
Institutional Planning and Operations
University Public Safety
